messages:
Evan Li: Heads-up: QA surfaced a weird customer flow where v1 clients hitting the API see a deprecation banner in the console but their route still resolves to v2 due to routing fallback. Tenants expect the banner to mean 'you're still on v1, upgrade later' not 'we routed you to v2'. We need clearer semantics.

Fiona Gupta: Ugh. That's confusing. Banner shows when tenant's default route is set to v1 but runtime routing policy did an emergency fallback to v2 for capacity. We never reflected fallback in console state. Should surface 'active route' vs 'configured route'.

Ben Rao: Agreed. From runtime side, we only emit a fallback event to the routing trace. Console currently reads config state from the control plane (configured route) not the active decision. Easy fix: add an active_route field to route-status API and to the tenant console.

Alice Chen: UX nuance: copy for banner needs to avoid alarming tenants. Maybe: "Your configured default is v1 (deprecated). Requests may temporarily be served by v2 due to capacity; consider testing on v2 or contact support." Keep it calm and actionable.

Evan Li: Also billing/quotas: if active route is v2 we might count against v2 quotas (or different quota bucket). Customers reported unexpected quota consumption against v2 quota even though they thought they were on v1. We must align quota attribution with active route.

Ben Rao: We currently attribute quota using the configured route header (X-Route-Config). That's the bug. Change: attribute on active decision emitted by the router. Router already writes a decision log with fields: decision_id, model_variant, reason. We'll surface model_variant for quota attribution.

Fiona Gupta: Telemetry needs to be updated: new metrics per-tenant: configured_route_pct, active_route_pct, fallback_reasons (list counts). Dashboards should show sudden spikes in active_route_pct to detect silent migration.

consolebot: Note: ticket #PLAT-3482 created (add active_route to route-status API + console display).

Alice Chen: In phased rollout we also want an opt-out for tenants who explicitly refuse auto-fallback. Proposal: per-tenant policy enum {ALLOW_FALLBACK, WARN_ONLY, DENY}. DENY returns 503 if configured route unavailable. WARN_ONLY does fallback but shows banner and notifies owners. ALLOW_FALLBACK silent. Default = WARN_ONLY for deprecated routes.

Ben Rao: Implementation details: router will check tenant.policy and attach X-Route-Decision: <model_variant> header. Quota service consumes X-Route-Decision if present, else X-Route-Config. We'll also record tenant.policy in admin audit logs.

Evan Li: Edge case: clients using SDK retries may see 503 -> SDK retries to v2 automatically causing weird UX. If tenant.policy == DENY we should have SDK-level guidance to not auto-upgrade. Add SDK note in deprecation doc.

Fiona Gupta: Console mock: show two pill states at top of tenant page: "Configured: v1-deprecated" and "Active: v2-stable" with timestamp of last decision and a small "why" link that opens routing trace. Banner text: "Active route differs from configured default due to capacity fallback. Click to view traces and options."

Ben Rao: Rollout plan: 1) Add active_route to route-status API (small schema change) + routing decision header (router) — internal canary. 2) Quota service change to prefer route-decision header. 3) Console reads active_route and shows pill + banner based on delta. 4) Add tenant.policy field and honor it in router. 5) Docs + SDK guidance. 6) Monitor configured/active mismatch metric and create alert if >5% tenants hit mismatches in <24h.

Evan Li: Backwards compatibility: older console versions will ignore active_route — that's ok. Routing header must be backward compatible. Use `X-Route-Decision-Version: 2` when present. If absent, existing behavior stays.

consolebot: deploybot started canary deploy of router v5 to cluster alpha with header enabled.

Alice Chen: Legal/CS: we need a short FAQ for customers who see "Configured v1 but Active v2". Avoid promising billing neutrality. Product suggestion: allow tenant to opt into "billing alignment mode" for 30 days (compute conversion factors) if they worry about tokenization differences during fallback.

Fiona Gupta: I'll mock the console pill and the small modal for routing traces. Ben, can you expose a simple /router/decision/<decision_id> debug endpoint with basic JSON for the modal? Keep it gated by a debug token in prod.

Ben Rao: Yup. I'll add a signed debug token requirement and TTL 5m so we don't leak traces. Also will emit decision_id in logs for SRE correlation.

Evan Li: OK timeline: canary router + header this week, quota switch next week (safe flag), console UI the week after. We'll run a 2-week canary then flip default. Who owns rollout doc?

Alice Chen: I'll own the rollout doc and create runbook entries for handling tenant complaints. I'll also coordinate messaging with growth/support.

consolebot: Reminder: Please add changelog entry for route-status API field addition.
